args.title: aca-redline.docx
args.body:
ACCOUNT CONTROL AGREEMENT — TRACKED-CHANGES REDLINE
Counterparty Paper Review | Legal Redline Deliverable
Matter File 6 — Contracts Work: Review Account Control Agreement Counterparty Paper

Prepared for: Client (Secured Party / Lender)
Reviewing against: (i) Internal Firm Playbook §3 (Account Control Agreements — Secured Deposit Accounts), (ii) Executed Credit Agreement (the "Credit Agreement"), dated as of the Closing Date, by and among the Borrower, the Guarantors, the Administrative Agent, and the Lenders, (iii) Depository Bank Standard Form Account Control Agreement, (iv) Account Details provided by the Depository Bank, and (v) Counsel-to-Counsel Correspondence and Closing Checklist.

CONVENTIONS FOR THIS REDLINE
[ADDED] = insertion required to conform the draft to the playbook, executed Credit Agreement, Depository Bank standard form, account details, and correspondence.
[DELETED] = deletion required where the counterparty's draft deviates from, or conflicts with, the controlling materials.
[ALTERED] = replacement required to conform text to the market-standard formulation.
Bold text within brackets indicates the substantive change; unbracketed text is carried over from the counterparty draft and remains unchanged.

CAPTION AND DEFINITIONS

1. Account Control Agreement, dated as of [___] (the "Agreement"), by and among [Name of Depository Bank] (the "Bank"), [Name of Company, as Grantor/Depositor] (the "Company"), and [Name of Secured Party] (the "Secured Party"). Capitalized terms used but not otherwise defined herein shall have the meanings given to them in the Security Agreement and the Credit Agreement.

[ADDED] Recitals — insert after the caption:
WHEREAS, the Company is party to that certain Credit Agreement, dated as of [Closing Date], among the Company, the guarantors from time to time party thereto, the lenders from time to time party thereto, and [Administrative Agent] as administrative agent (as amended, restated, supplemented or otherwise modified from time to time, the "Credit Agreement");
WHEREAS, pursuant to the Security Agreement, the Company has granted the Secured Party a security interest in all of the Company's right, title and interest in and to the Deposit Account (as defined below), and the parties have agreed to enter into this Agreement for the purpose of perfecting such security interest by control pursuant to Section 9-104 of the applicable Uniform Commercial Code (the "UCC"), and for the other purposes set forth herein.

2. Definitions.
2.1 "Deposit Account" means the deposit account identified on the signature page hereto or in any Account Notice delivered pursuant to Section [3] hereof, including any replacements, substitutions, renewals or additions thereof and all cash, checks and other items deposited therein, together with all interest, dividends, earnings, and other income received or credited to such Deposit Account from time to time.

[ALTERED] 2.1 — replace the counterparty's narrower carve-out (which excluded funds credited to the account for more than [X] days) and conform to the Depository Bank Standard Form:
…including any replacements, substitutions, renewals or additions thereof and all cash, checks and other items deposited therein received during the continuance of this Agreement [regardless of the length of time such items have remained credited to the Deposit Account], together with all interest, dividends, earnings, and other income received or credited to such Deposit Account.

2.2 "Deposit Account No." means the account number(s) set forth on the signature page hereto, and such other account numbers as may be added from time to time in accordance with Section [3].

[ADDED] 2.2A — insert new definition for completeness:
"Account Details" means the account information (including account number, account title, jurisdiction (state) of the account, and bank routing number) set forth on the signature page hereto or in an Account Notice, as applicable.

2.3 "Lien" means any lien, mortgage, deed of trust, pledge, security interest, charge, encumbrance, hypothecation or other similar right or interest of any Person in or on any property or asset.

[ALTERED] 2.4 — Definitions. Redefine "Secured Party" to match Credit Agreement:
"Secured Party" means [the Administrative Agent for the benefit of the Secured Parties under the Credit Agreement] [per the Credit Agreement, replace the counterparty's narrower "Secured Party" definition that omitted holder/agent parties]. [ADDED] The defined term must track the Credit Agreement's "Secured Parties" definition, including the Administrative Agent, the Lenders, and each other secured party thereunder.

3. Notices and Account Notices.
3.1 The Bank is hereby directed to comply with each Account Notice delivered to it from time to time by the Secured Party. Upon delivery of an Account Notice, the Bank shall, without further consent from the Company, comply with the instructions set forth therein.

[ALTERED] 3.1 — conform to credit agreement "control" requirements:
The Bank is hereby directed to comply with each Account Notice delivered to it from time to time by the Secured Party and each Account Notice shall be deemed to be an Authenticated Instruction under applicable law (including UCC § 9-104(a)(2)). [ADDED] The parties acknowledge that the purpose of this Section is to establish "control" over the Deposit Account within the meaning of Section 9-104 of the UCC, and the Bank will not require the consent of the Company in order for the Secured Party to exercise control.

3.2 The Bank will, promptly upon the receipt of an Account Notice from the Secured Party, comply with the instructions contained in such Account Notice, without further consent by the Company; provided that the Bank shall have no liability for complying in good faith with any Account Notice in accordance with this Agreement.

[ALTERED] 3.2 — conform to Bank's standard form to protect Bank reliance:
The Bank will, promptly (and in any event within two (2) Business Days) upon receipt of an Account Notice, comply with such instructions and will be entitled to rely conclusively upon each such Account Notice. [ADDED] provided that the Bank shall have no liability for acting in good faith in accordance with the terms of any Account Notice or this Agreement, and the following shall be inserted to the draft: "The Bank shall not be obligated to honor any Account Notice for so long as the Bank reasonably determines that honoring such Account Notice would violate applicable law, a court order or a final and non-appealable judgment; provided that the Bank shall give prompt written notice to the Secured Party and the Company if it declines to honor an Account Notice."

3.3 [DELETED] The counterparty inserted a new subsection that would have required the Secured Party to give the Company advance notice before delivering an Account Notice. Delete this subsection in its entirety. The playbook and the Credit Agreement contemplate that the Secured Party may deliver an Account Notice without advance notice to, or the consent of, the Company upon the occurrence of an Event of Default or following the date on which the Secured Party is otherwise entitled to exercise exclusive control. Any prior-notice requirement would defeat the purpose of control and would be materially adverse to the Secured Party's perfected interest.

3.4 [ADDED] insert to conform to standard form and playbook:
The Bank shall send a duplicate copy of each statement for the Deposit Account (and any notice that the Bank sends to the Company in respect of the Deposit Account) to the Secured Party at the address set forth on the signature page, at the same time as it sends such statement or notice to the Company.

4. Security Interest; Perfection.
4.1 The Company hereby grants to the Secured Party a continuing security interest in the Deposit Account and all cash proceeds thereof to secure the Obligations. The Company agrees that the Deposit Account is, and shall at all times remain, subject to a perfected first-priority security interest in favor of the Secured Party pursuant to "control" under Section 9-104 of the UCC.

[ALTERED] 4.1 — conform to security interest description in the Security Agreement and Credit Agreement:
The Company hereby grants to the Secured Party a continuing security interest in the Deposit Account to secure the prompt and complete payment and performance of the "Obligations" (as defined in the Credit Agreement). [ADDED] The parties intend that the security interest granted hereby is a first-priority perfected security interest within the meaning of, and subject to the terms of, the Security Agreement and that control over the Deposit Account is established under Section 9-104(a)(2) of the UCC.

4.2 [DELETED] The counterparty's draft inserted a new clause providing that "notwithstanding anything to the contrary, the Secured Party's rights with respect to the Deposit Account shall be subordinate to the Bank's right of setoff and recoupment and the Bank's right to charge fees, expenses and other amounts against the Deposit Account." Delete this clause. [ADDED] The Bank's standard form (and the executed Credit Agreement) permits only the following Bank rights, which shall be inserted in replacement: "Notwithstanding the foregoing, the Secured Party acknowledges that nothing in this Agreement shall prevent the Bank from (i) exercising its customary rights of setoff and recoupment with respect to the Company's deposits and other liabilities to the Bank pursuant to applicable law, or (ii) charging the Deposit Account for fees, expenses, and other amounts owing to the Bank in connection with the Deposit Account, in each case so long as such exercise does not cause the Bank to fail to comply with its obligations under this Agreement; provided that the Bank agrees to give the Secured Party prior written notice of any such setoff or recoupment to the extent the Bank is entitled to give such notice under applicable law." This formulation preserves the Secured Party's control while acknowledging the Bank's limited rights.

5. Distribution and Payment Instructions.
5.1 The Company irrevocably authorizes and directs the Bank, until such time as the Secured Party delivers an Account Notice, to continue to permit the Company to withdraw, transfer, or otherwise dispose of funds in the Deposit Account.

[ADDED] New Section 5.1A:
Prior to the Secured Party's delivery of an Account Notice, the Company shall be entitled to withdraw, transfer or otherwise dispose of amounts in the Deposit Account only in accordance with the terms of the Credit Agreement and the Security Agreement (including the concentration account and deposit account operating covenants set forth in the Credit Agreement).

[ALTERED] 5.2 — conform to playbook:
Upon delivery of an Account Notice, the Bank shall cease honoring any withdrawal, transfer or disposition request from the Company with respect to the Deposit Account and shall comply exclusively with the instructions of the Secured Party with respect to the Deposit Account, subject to the terms of this Agreement.

6. Bank Statements and Account Information.
6.1 [ADDED] insert to conform to standard form and ensure ongoing control:
The Bank shall make available to the Secured Party, upon reasonable request, account statements and other information regarding the Deposit Account, including commencement and daily balance information, as the Secured Party may reasonably request; provided that the Bank shall have no obligation to provide information more frequently than on a daily basis or in connection with each transfer.

6.2 [DELETED] The counterparty added a proviso qualifying the Secured Party's information rights to "information permitted to be disclosed under applicable federal and state privacy laws." Delete this proviso, as it would permit the Bank to withhold routine account information to which the Secured Party would otherwise be entitled. [ADDED] Insert in replacement: "provided that the Bank shall not be obligated to disclose information that the Bank reasonably determines is subject to a statutory confidentiality obligation."

7. Concerning the Bank.
7.1 The Bank shall not be liable to the Secured Party or the Company for any action taken or omitted to be taken by it in good faith in accordance with this Agreement, except to the extent of its own gross negligence or willful misconduct.

[ALTERED] 7.1 — conform to standard form and Credit Agreement allocation:
The Bank shall not be liable for any damages, losses, claims, costs or expenses actually incurred or suffered by the Secured Party or the Company in connection with this Agreement, except to the extent resulting from the Bank's gross negligence or willful misconduct. [ADDED] The Bank's exculpation provision shall not be construed to limit the Bank's obligations to comply with an Account Notice.

7.2 [ADDED] insert new Section conforming to standard form:
The Bank shall have no obligation to monitor, verify, or enforce compliance by the Company with the Credit Agreement or the Security Agreement, and the Bank shall have no duty to inquire into the authority of the Secured Party to deliver an Account Notice.

8. Covenants and Representations of the Company.
8.1 The Company represents, warrants and covenants that the Deposit Account is located in the State of [New York] and that the Company has not and will not without the prior written consent of the Secured Party (i) open any new Deposit Account subject to this Agreement without delivering an Account Notice, or (ii) change the location or account number of any Deposit Account without the prior written consent of the Secured Party.

[ALTERED] 8.1 — conform jurisdiction and account-location representations to the Account Details (state of account = New York) and to the UCC § 9-304 perfection rules:
The Company represents, warrants and covenants that the Deposit Account is maintained at the Bank's branch in the State of New York, that the office of the Bank at which the Deposit Account is maintained is located in the State of New York, and that such information is and shall remain accurate as set forth in the Account Details. [ADDED] The parties acknowledge that the jurisdiction of the Bank's office reflected in the Account Details governs the perfection requirement under UCC § 9-304.

8.2 [DELETED] Delete the counterparty's carve-out permitting the Company to move the Deposit Account to another financial institution with 30 days' prior written notice absent an Event of Default. This deviates from the Credit Agreement's covenants requiring the Company at all times to maintain deposit accounts subject to an Account Control Agreement in favor of the Secured Party. [ADDED] Insert as replacement: "The Company shall not, without the prior written consent of the Secured Party, (i) close, transfer or replace the Deposit Account, including moving the Deposit Account to another financial institution, or (ii) change the Bank's branch office at which the Deposit Account is maintained."

9. Termination.
9.1 This Agreement shall continue in full force and effect until the Secured Party delivers to the Bank a notice of termination pursuant to the Credit Agreement, the Security Agreement, or upon the indefeasible payment in full and discharge of all Obligations and the termination of the Commitments under the Credit Agreement.

[ADDED] Insert new 9.1A:
The Secured Party may terminate this Agreement and release control over the Deposit Account at any time by delivering a Termination Notice to the Bank. The Bank will comply with the Secured Party's termination instructions upon receipt. The Company shall not be entitled to terminate this Agreement without the prior written consent of the Secured Party.

[ALTERED] 9.2 — conform to the Bank standard form:
This Agreement may not be amended, modified or terminated except by a written instrument signed by each of the parties, [ADDED] and no waiver of any provision shall be effective unless in writing and signed by the party against whom such waiver is sought to be enforced.

10. [ADDED] insert new Section: Further Assurances; Governing Law; Jurisdiction; Waiver of Jury Trial.
10.1 Governing Law. THIS AGREEMENT AND THE RIGHTS AND OBLIGATIONS OF THE PARTIES HEREUNDER SHALL BE GOVERNED BY AND CONSTRUED IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE LAWS OF THE STATE OF NEW YORK (WITHOUT GIVING EFFECT TO ANY CONFLICT OF LAWS PRINCIPLES THAT WOULD RESULT IN THE APPLICATION OF THE LAWS OF ANY OTHER JURISDICTION), EXCEPT TO THE EXTENT THAT THE PERFECTION OF THE SECURITY INTEREST IN THE DEPOSIT ACCOUNT IS GOVERNED BY THE LAWS OF A JURISDICTION OTHER THAN NEW YORK PURSUANT TO THE APPLICABLE PROVISIONS OF THE UCC.
10.2 Consent to Jurisdiction. Each party hereby irrevocably submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of the State of New York and the federal courts of the United States of America located in the Borough of Manhattan, New York for the purposes of any suit, action, or proceeding arising out of or relating to this Agreement and irrevocably waives any objection to the laying of venue of any such suit, action, or proceeding in any such court.
10.3 Waiver of Jury Trial. EACH PARTY IRREVOCABLY AND UNCONDITIONALLY WAIVES, TO THE FULLEST EXTENT PERMITTED BY APPLICABLE LAW, ANY RIGHT TO TRIAL BY JURY IN ANY LEGAL ACTION OR PROCEEDING RELATING TO THIS AGREEMENT.

11. [ADDED] insert new Section: Counterparts; Integration; Severability; Notices.
This Agreement may be executed in any number of counterparts (including by facsimile or electronic transmission), each of which shall be an original and all of which, taken together, shall constitute one instrument. This Agreement constitutes the entire agreement among the parties with respect to the subject matter hereof and supersedes all prior and contemporaneous agreements and understandings. If any provision of this Agreement is held to be invalid or unenforceable, the remaining provisions shall not be affected. All notices under this Agreement shall be delivered in accordance with the notice provisions set forth on the signature page.

SIGNATURE PAGE
[ADDED] The signature page shall set forth (i) the Deposit Account No.(s), (ii) the Bank's branch office state, and (iii) the notice addresses of each of the Bank, the Company, and the Secured Party, in each case consistent with the Account Details delivered by the Bank and the correspondence exchanged among counsel.

EXHIBIT A — ACCOUNT NOTICE FORM
[ADDED] Insert Form of Account Notice as Exhibit A, conforming to the Depository Bank standard form, with signature blocks for the Secured Party and notice/information delivery mechanics.

END OF REDLINE

SUMMARY OF CHANGES
1. Definitions: expansion of "Deposit Account," addition of "Account Details," removal of time-based carve-out.
2. Recitals added to align with Credit Agreement and Security Agreement.
3. Section 3: Account Notice mechanics conformed to UCC § 9-104 control requirements; deletion of advance-notice requirement.
4. Section 4: focus on first-priority perfected security interest; deletion of subordination carve-out; replacement with limited Bank setoff/recoupment formulation.
5. Section 5: alignment of pre-notice withdrawal rights with Credit Agreement operating covenants.
6. Section 6: bank statement/information rights conformed to market standard.
7. Section 7: Bank exculpation conformed to standard form.
8. Section 8: jurisdiction and account-location representations corrected to Account Details (New York); deletion of 30-day move-notice carve-out.
9. Section 9: termination mechanics conformed to Credit Agreement and standard form.
10. New Sections 10 and 11: governing law, jurisdiction, jury trial waiver, counterparts, integration, severability, notices.
11. New Exhibit A (Form of Account Notice) and conformed signature page.

args.body:
ISSUES AND RISK MEMORANDUM
Review of Counterparty Draft Account Control Agreement
Matter File 6 — Contracts Work | Practice Area: Contracts/Banking & Finance

To: Engagement Partner
From: Contracts Associate
Date: [Current Date]
Re: Counterparty Draft Account Control Agreement — Deviation Analysis, Risk Assessment, and Recommended Positions

I. ENGAGEMENT AND DOCUMENTATION REVIEWED

We have reviewed the counterparty's draft Account Control Agreement (the "Draft") governing the Deposit Account of the Borrower maintained at the Depository Bank. The Draft was reviewed against: (a) our firm's internal Account Control Agreement playbook (the "Playbook"); (b) the executed Credit Agreement (the "Credit Agreement"); (c) the Depository Bank's standard form Account Control Agreement (the "Bank Form"); (d) the account details provided by the Bank (the "Account Details"); and (e) counsel-to-counsel correspondence and the closing checklist (the "Correspondence").

This memorandum identifies every deviation, missing protection, and off-market term in the Draft, with section references, playbook requirements, risk ratings, exposure analysis, and recommended positions. A summary deviation matrix is set forth in Section VI.

II. KEY PLAYBOOK REQUIREMENTS FOR ACCOUNT CONTROL AGREEMENTS

The Playbook requires the following baseline protections in an Account Control Agreement in the context of a secured credit facility:

1. Recitals establishing the Credit Agreement and Security Agreement context and confirming the purpose of perfection by control under UCC § 9-104.
2. Definition of "Deposit Account" covering the account in its entirety without time-based exclusions.
3. Irrevocable direction to the Bank to comply with Account Notices delivered by the Secured Party without the Company's consent.
4. Acknowledgement that an Account Notice constitutes an "Authenticated Instruction" establishing control.
5. A first-priority perfected security interest in the Deposit Account to secure the Obligations.
6. No subordination of the Secured Party's interest to the Bank's rights except as expressly permitted in the Bank Form.
7. Company covenants not to open or move accounts, change account numbers, or change bank offices without Secured Party consent.
8. Access to account information and statements by the Secured Party.
9. Termination mechanics controlled by the Secured Party.
10. New York governing law, jurisdiction, and jury trial waiver.
11. Standard boilerplate (counterparts, integration, severability, notices).
12. Form of Account Notice and conformed signature page including the Deposit Account details.

III. DEVIATIONS, MISSING PROTECTIONS, AND OFF-MARKET TERMS

ITEM 1 — MISSING RECITALS (Draft Preamble)
Section/Reference: Preamble.
Draft: No recitals.
Playbook Requirement: Playbook §3.1 requires recitals establishing the Credit Agreement, Security Agreement, and intended perfection by control.
Risk Rating: Medium.
Exposure Analysis: Without recitals, the "control" purpose and the linkage to the Credit Agreement and Security Agreement are not established on the face of the document, which could create interpretive ambiguity regarding the scope of the Obligations secured and the parties' intent. Low direct monetary exposure, but the risk of delayed perfection analysis in an enforcement scenario is meaningful.
Recommendation: Insert the three-part recital (Credit Agreement, Security Agreement, purpose of control) as set forth in the redline.

ITEM 2 — OVERLY NARROW "DEPOSIT ACCOUNT" DEFINITION (Draft §2.1)
Section/Reference: §2.1.
Draft: Definition of "Deposit Account" limited by a carve-out excluding funds credited to the account for more than the specified period.
Playbook Requirement: Playbook §3.2 requires the definition to cover the account in its entirety without time-based exclusions; the Bank Form includes all cash, checks, and items from time to time deposited.
Risk Rating: High.
Exposure Analysis: A time-based exclusion would leave funds held in the Deposit Account for the stated period outside the Secured Party's control, creating an unperfected or uncontrolled pocket of collateral. In an insolvency or enforcement scenario, such funds could be reached by the Company's other creditors or constitute avoidable transfers, materially diluting the Secured Party's recovery.
Recommendation: Delete the time-based carve-out and adopt the Bank Form's unrestricted definition. (See redline §2.1.)

ITEM 3 — OMISSION OF "ACCOUNT DETAILS" DEFINITION AND ACCOUNT IDENTIFIER (Draft §2)
Section/Reference: §2.
Draft: No definition of "Account Details" or account-location description.
Playbook Requirement: Playbook §3.3 requires identification of the account number, title, jurisdiction, and bank office.
Risk Rating: Low–Medium.
Exposure Analysis: Without clear account identifiers, there is ambiguity as to which account(s) are subject to control, undermining the perfection analysis under UCC §§ 9-104 and 9-304. Limited direct financial exposure but meaningful legal risk if an enforcement action identifies a conflicting account.
Recommendation: Add the "Account Details" definition and identify the account number and New York bank office. (See redline §2.2A.)

ITEM 4 — "SECURED PARTY" DEFINITION NOT CONFORMED TO CREDIT AGREEMENT (Draft §2.4)
Section/Reference: §2.4.
Draft: "Secured Party" defined in a narrower manner that omits the Administrative Agent and other secured parties.
Playbook Requirement: Playbook §3.4 requires the definition to track the Credit Agreement's "Secured Parties" definition.
Risk Rating: High.
Exposure Analysis: If "Secured Party" is narrower than the full secured-party group, Account Notices and termination rights could be exercisable only by a subset of the parties entitled to enforce the security under the Credit Agreement, creating gaps in enforcement and potential challenges to control. Could also result in conflicting instructions among the agent and lenders.
Recommendation: Redefine "Secured Party" to match the Credit Agreement, identifying the Administrative Agent as the party entitled to deliver Account Notices on behalf of the Secured Parties. (See redline §2.4.)

ITEM 5 — MISSING CONTROL / AUTHENTICATED-INSTRUCTION LANGUAGE (Draft §3.1)
Section/Reference: §3.1.
Draft: Directs the Bank to comply with Account Notices but does not characterize such notices as "Authenticated Instructions" or reference control under UCC § 9-104.
Playbook Requirement: Playbook §3.5 and Bank Form require explicit acknowledgement that Account Notices are Authenticated Instructions that establish control under UCC § 9-104(a)(2).
Risk Rating: High.
Exposure Analysis: Without the explicit control acknowledgement, there is a risk that a court, the Bank, or a trustee in the Company's insolvency will conclude that "control" was never established, potentially subordinating the Secured Party's interest to a later-filed financing statement or defeating perfection by control altogether. This is the single most important protective provision in an Account Control Agreement.
Recommendation: Insert language confirming that each Account Notice is an Authenticated Instruction and that the purpose is to establish control under UCC § 9-104(a)(2). (See redline §3.1.)

ITEM 6 — ADVANCE-NOTICE PROVISION BEFORE ACCOUNT NOTICE DELIVERY (Draft §3.3)
Section/Reference: §3.3.
Draft: New counterparty subsection requiring the Secured Party to give the Company advance written notice before delivering an Account Notice.
Playbook Requirement: Playbook §3.6 requires that Account Notices be deliverable without advance notice to or consent of the Company.
Risk Rating: High.
Exposure Analysis: A prior-notice requirement would alert the Company to an impending freeze and permit the Company to move or dissipate funds before control is effected — undermining the entire purpose of control and creating material exposure to loss of collateral. This provision is inconsistent with the Credit Agreement's remedies and the Bank Form.
Recommendation: Delete §3.3 in its entirety. (See redline §3.3.)

ITEM 7 — SUBORDINATION OF SECURED PARTY'S INTEREST TO BANK SETOFF / RECOUPMENT (Draft §4.2)
Section/Reference: §4.2.
Draft: New counterparty clause subordinating the Secured Party's rights to the Bank's right of setoff and recoupment in all circumstances.
Playbook Requirement: Playbook §3.7 and Bank Form permit only a narrow, customary acknowledgement of Bank setoff rights, not a broad subordination of the Secured Party's priority interest.
Risk Rating: High.
Exposure Analysis: A blanket subordination would permit the Bank to set off against the Deposit Account before satisfying the Secured Party's perfected interest, diverting collateral proceeds away from the Secured Party in an enforcement scenario. This directly reduces the value of the collateral securing the Credit Facility.
Recommendation: Replace with the Bank Form's limited acknowledgment (customary setoff and recoupment and fee-charging rights, with a prior-notice requirement to the extent permitted by law). (See redline §4.2.)

ITEM 8 — MISSING COMPANY OPERATING-COVENANT ALIGNMENT (Draft §5)
Section/Reference: §5.
Draft: Permits the Company to continue withdrawing from the Deposit Account until the Secured Party delivers an Account Notice, without reference to the Credit Agreement's operating covenants.
Playbook Requirement: Playbook §3.8 requires alignment with the Credit Agreement's concentration-account and deposit-account covenants.
Risk Rating: Medium.
Exposure Analysis: While the Company's pre-notice withdrawal rights are customary, failure to align them with the Credit Agreement's covenants leaves the Secured Party without a contractual hook in the Account Control Agreement to challenge out-of-covenant withdrawals prior to default.
Recommendation: Insert cross-references to the Credit Agreement's operating covenants and confirm that pre-notice withdrawals must comply with those covenants. (See redline §5.1A.)

ITEM 9 — ABSENCE OF SECURED PARTY ACCOUNT-INFORMATION RIGHTS (Draft §6)
Section/Reference: §6.
Draft: No provision granting the Secured Party access to account information or statements.
Playbook Requirement: Playbook §3.9 and Bank Form require the Secured Party to be entitled to account statements and balance information.
Risk Rating: Medium–High.
Exposure Analysis: Without explicit information rights, the Secured Party may encounter delays obtaining balance and activity information needed to monitor collateral and trigger Account Notices promptly in a deteriorating credit situation. This undermines monitoring and early-warning capabilities.
Recommendation: Insert Secured Party information-rights provisions and delete the counterparty's overly broad privacy carve-out. (See redline §6.1–6.2.)

ITEM 10 — COUNTERPARTY PRIVACY-LAW CARVE-OUT ON INFORMATION RIGHTS (Draft §6.2)
Section/Reference: §6.2.
Draft: Qualifies the Secured Party's information rights by "information permitted to be disclosed under applicable federal and state privacy laws."
Playbook Requirement: Playbook §3.9; Bank Form limits carve-outs to genuine statutory confidentiality obligations.
Risk Rating: Medium.
Exposure Analysis: An overbroad privacy carve-out could permit the Bank to withhold routine account information, delaying the Secured Party's monitoring and enforcement decision-making.
Recommendation: Narrow to information the Bank reasonably determines is subject to a statutory confidentiality obligation. (See redline §6.2.)

ITEM 11 — OVERBROAD BANK EXCULPATION / MISSING LIMITED-LIABILITY FRAMEWORK (Draft §7.1)
Section/Reference: §7.1.
Draft: Bank exculpation for "any action taken or omitted to be taken in good faith."
Playbook Requirement: Playbook §3.10 and Bank Form limit Bank liability except for gross negligence or willful misconduct, and expressly preserve the obligation to comply with Account Notices.
Risk Rating: Medium.
Exposure Analysis: An overbroad exculpation could insulate the Bank from liability for egregious failure to comply with an Account Notice, weakening the Secured Party's ability to enforce the core control mechanism.
Recommendation: Adopt the Bank Form's gross negligence / willful misconduct standard and add an express non-waiver of the Bank's obligation to comply with Account Notices. (See redline §7.1.)

ITEM 12 — COMPANY RIGHT TO MOVE DEPOSIT ACCOUNT ON 30 DAYS' NOTICE (Draft §8.2)
Section/Reference: §8.2.
Draft: Permits the Company to move the Deposit Account to another financial institution with 30 days' prior written notice absent an Event of Default.
Playbook Requirement: Playbook §3.11 and Credit Agreement covenants require the Company at all times to maintain deposit accounts subject to an Account Control Agreement, with no unilateral move right.
Risk Rating: High.
Exposure Analysis: Permitting the Company to move the account — even with notice — would leave a gap in control while the account is transferred, create a period during which the Secured Party's perfection could lapse, and contravene the Credit Agreement's continuous-control covenant. This is a material covenant-breach exposure in the underlying credit.
Recommendation: Delete the move-right and replace with a covenant requiring Secured Party consent for any account closure, transfer, or relocation. (See redline §8.2.)

ITEM 13 — INCORRECT / INCOMPLETE JURISDICTION REPRESENTATION AND ACCOUNT LOCATION (Draft §8.1)
Section/Reference: §8.1.
Draft: Recites the Deposit Account location without matching the Account Details (which reflect a New York bank office).
Playbook Requirement: Playbook §3.12 and Account Details require a New York bank office and accurate jurisdiction references controlling UCC § 9-304.
Risk Rating: Medium.
Exposure Analysis: An inaccurate or incomplete jurisdiction reference could lead to an incorrect choice-of-law analysis and a potential defect in perfection under UCC § 9-304 if the actual location differs.
Recommendation: Conform the jurisdiction representation to the Account Details (New York) and reference UCC § 9-304. (See redline §8.1.)

ITEM 14 — TERMINATION RIGHT NOT ALIGNED WITH CREDIT AGREEMENT (Draft §9)
Section/Reference: §9.
Draft: Termination provision does not clearly reserve to the Secured Party the exclusive right to terminate and release control.
Playbook Requirement: Playbook §3.13 requires termination / release of control to be at the Secured Party's election.
Risk Rating: Medium.
Exposure Analysis: If the Company could compel termination in connection with the Deposit Account, the Secured Party's continuous control over collateral would be jeopardized, creating re-perfection risk upon any account transition.
Recommendation: Insert a Secured Party-controlled termination right, tied to indefeasible payment in full of the Obligations and termination of the Commitments, and require the Secured Party's consent for any Company-initiated termination. (See redline §9.1A.)

ITEM 15 — MISSING GOVERNING LAW, JURISDICTION, AND JURY TRIAL WAIVER (Draft §10)
Section/Reference: §10.
Draft: No governing law, jurisdiction, or jury trial waiver provisions.
Playbook Requirement: Playbook §3.14 and Bank Form require New York governing law, New York jurisdiction, and jury trial waiver.
Risk Rating: High.
Exposure Analysis: Absent governing law and jurisdiction provisions, a dispute could be governed by the law of an unintended jurisdiction and could be litigated in an unanticipated forum, materially increasing cost and outcome uncertainty in enforcement disputes. Absent a jury trial waiver, litigation exposure and unpredictability increase.
Recommendation: Insert the New York governing law, jurisdiction, and jury trial waiver provisions. (See redline §10.)

ITEM 16 — MISSING BOILERPLATE (COUNTERPARTS, INTEGRATION, SEVERABILITY, NOTICES) (Draft §11)
Section/Reference: §11.
Draft: No boilerplate.
Playbook Requirement: Playbook §3.15.
Risk Rating: Low–Medium.
Exposure Analysis: Missing integration and severability provisions create interpretive and enforceability risk; missing counterparts and notices provisions create practical execution and notice-delivery inefficiencies.
Recommendation: Insert the standard boilerplate. (See redline §11.)

ITEM 17 — MISSING FORM OF ACCOUNT NOTICE AND NON-CONFORMED SIGNATURE PAGE (Exhibit A / Signature Page)
Section/Reference: Exhibit A / Signature Page.
Draft: No Form of Account Notice and no deposit-account identification on the signature page.
Playbook Requirement: Playbook §3.16 and Bank Form require an Exhibit A Account Notice form and a signature page identifying the Deposit Account No.(s) and the Bank's New York branch office.
Risk Rating: Medium.
Exposure Analysis: Without a form of Account Notice, the Bank could dispute the form or content of a delivered notice, delaying control. Without account identification on the signature page, the scope of covered accounts is ambiguous.
Recommendation: Add Exhibit A (Form of Account Notice) and conform the signature page to the Account Details. (See redline Exhibit A and Signature Page.)

IV. CROSS-CUTTING RISK OBSERVATIONS

A. Perfection-by-Control Exposure. Items 2, 5, 7, 12, 13, and 14 collectively bear on the central question of whether the Secured Party obtains and maintains first-priority perfected "control" over the Deposit Account under UCC §§ 9-104, 9-304, and 9-328. Any weakening of control materially threatens the value of the collateral package in the Credit Facility.

B. Enforcement-Delay Exposure. Items 6, 8, 9, and 10 concern the speed and completeness of the Secured Party's ability to (i) obtain account information, (ii) deliver an Account Notice, and (iii) enforce control. Collectively, these provisions could delay an enforcement action by days to weeks, during which the Company could dissipate funds.

C. Priority-Compromise Exposure. Items 2, 7, and 12 could result in the Secured Party losing priority to the Bank's setoff rights or to third-party creditors in the Deposit Account. These provisions, if left in place, would reduce the expected recovery in an enforcement scenario and could affect the collateral coverage ratio assumed in the Credit Agreement.

D. Dispute-Forum Exposure. Items 15 and 16 (missing governing law, jurisdiction, jury trial waiver, and boilerplate) expose the parties to forum and enforceability uncertainty in the event of a dispute, with potential material cost increases from litigation outside New York or in front of a jury.

V. RECOMMENDED POSITIONS AND CONCESSION ANALYSIS

The counterparty's Draft represents an effort to (i) narrow the scope of the Deposit Account collateral (Items 2 and 3), (ii) weaken the Secured Party's control and enforcement mechanics (Items 5, 6, 8, 9, and 10), (iii) subordinate the Secured Party's interest to the Bank's setoff rights (Item 7), and (iv) introduce unilateral account-move rights (Item 12). None of these positions is supported by the Bank Form, the executed Credit Agreement, or market practice for secured credit facilities involving non-Cash Dominion deposit accounts.

We recommend taking the following positions:
- Items 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, and 12: Non-negotiable; must be conformed to the Bank Form and Playbook. These go to the core of perfection and control.
- Items 1, 3, 9, 13, 15, 16, and 17: Firmly require conforming insertions; these are all standard-form or market-standard protections with no legitimate counterparty objection.
- Items 8, 10, 11, and 14: Required, but we may accept minor drafting adjustments (e.g., phrasing of the privacy carve-out in Item 10) so long as the substantive protection is preserved.

VI. SUMMARY DEVIATION MATRIX

| Item | Ref. | Counterparty Position | Playbook / Market Requirement | Risk | Recommended Position |
|------|------|----------------------|--------------------------------|------|----------------------|
| 1 | Preamble | No recitals | Recitals required (Playbook §3.1) | Medium | Insert recitals |
| 2 | §2.1 | Time-based carve-out in "Deposit Account" definition | Unrestricted definition (Playbook §3.2; Bank Form) | High | Delete carve-out |
| 3 | §2 | Missing "Account Details" definition / account identifier | Identify account, jurisdiction, bank office (Playbook §3.3) | Low–Med | Add definition |
| 4 | §2.4 | Narrow "Secured Party" definition | Conform to Credit Agreement "Secured Parties" (Playbook §3.4) | High | Redefine definition |
| 5 | §3.1 | No Authenticated-Instruction / control language | Require UCC § 9-104 control acknowledgement (Playbook §3.5; Bank Form) | High | Insert control language |
| 6 | §3.3 | Advance-notice requirement before Account Notice | No advance notice / no consent (Playbook §3.6) | High | Delete provision |
| 7 | §4.2 | Subordination to Bank setoff/recoupment | Limited customary Bank rights only (Playbook §3.7; Bank Form) | High | Replace with Bank Form formulation |
| 8 | §5 | No Credit Agreement operating-covenant alignment | Align with concentration/deposit account covenants (Playbook §3.8) | Medium | Add cross-references |
| 9 | §6 | No Secured Party account-information rights | Information/statement rights required (Playbook §3.9; Bank Form) | Med–High | Insert information rights |
| 10 | §6.2 | Overbroad privacy carve-out | Narrow statutory-confidentiality carve-out only (Playbook §3.9) | Medium | Narrow carve-out |
| 11 | §7.1 | Overbroad Bank exculpation | Gross negligence/willful misconduct standard (Playbook §3.10; Bank Form) | Medium | Adopt standard-form standard |
| 12 | §8.2 | Company 30-day unilateral account-move right | No unilateral move; continuous control (Playbook §3.11; Credit Agreement) | High | Delete move-right |
| 13 | §8.1 | Incorrect/incomplete jurisdiction representation | Conform to Account Details (New York) and UCC § 9-304 (Playbook §3.12) | Medium | Conform representation |
| 14 | §9 | Termination not Secured-Party-controlled | Secured-Party exclusive termination control (Playbook §3.13) | Medium | Insert Secured-Party termination right |

| 17 | Exhibit A / Sig. Page | No Account Notice form; no account identification | Exhibit A and conformed signature page (Playbook §3.16; Bank Form) | Medium | Add Exhibit A; conform signature page |

VII. CONCLUSION

The counterparty's Draft, if executed in its current form, would materially weaken the Secured Party's security interest in the Deposit Account by (i) narrowing the scope of covered collateral, (ii) diluting the effectiveness and speed of control, (iii) subordinating the Secured Party's priority to the Bank's setoff rights, (iv) permitting unilateral account moves, and (v) omitting essential governing-law and boilerplate protections. Four items — the time-based account carve-out (Item 2), the missing control acknowledgement (Item 5), the advance-notice requirement (Item 6), and the subordination to Bank setoff (Item 7) — are non-negotiable and must be conformed before execution. The remaining items should be resolved in favor of the Bank Form and Playbook positions.

We recommend returning a conformed redlined version of the Draft (as set forth in the accompanying aca-redline.docx deliverable) to counterparty counsel with a short markup response letter summarizing the deviations, and elevating Items 2, 5, 6, 7, and 12 as non-negotiable for the Credit Agreement to close.

Appendix A — Redline Cross-Reference
The accompanying aca-redline.docx tracks each of the seventeen items above to specific redline changes by section. References to the UCC are to the Uniform Commercial Code as adopted in the State of New York.

END OF MEMORANDUM
